promptAsSent:
Use the image_gen tool to generate exactly one image, then stop. Do not write files, run commands or edit anything.

Attached reference images, in order:
Image 1: INPUT 1: the render to repaint (layout authority)
Image 2: INPUT 2: the fighter's livery (colours only)

Use case: precise-object-edit / texture reskin of a technical 3D render.
INPUT 1 is a render of a 3D model of one small single-seat space fighter, a Talon interceptor about 12 metres long, seen from above its port bow quarter on a plain light grey background. Its flat colours mark which material each surface is: dull red armour plates (the cockpit pod, the gun nacelle, the aft body and the two wing plates), dark grey steel structure (the two drive drums at the stern, the centre spine between the pods, the canopy frame and the gun housing), bright steel rings and lips, near-black recesses, vents and grilles, and a cyan-tinted canopy. The fighter stands on two sled runners under the hull: dark grey steel runners and struts with near-black clamps and pads; its wing plates droop outboard and its noses droop.
INPUT 2 is a painted top-down illustration of this exact fighter in its livery: use it ONLY for the paint scheme and colours. Never copy its view, composition, shapes or illustration style.

Repaint the fighter in INPUT 1 as a real, photographed spacecraft in that livery. This image fixes the paint, finish and wear standard for the whole model, so:
- Geometry must not move. Keep the fighter exactly where it is, the same size, same silhouette and outline, same camera, every plate, vent, grille, ring and the canopy in exactly the same pixels. Do not zoom, crop, shift, rotate or redraw any shape. Background stays the same plain flat light grey with no floor, shadow, stars, text or border.
- Keep every surface's material: red armour plates become a slightly warm, mid-saturated red enamel (as INPUT 2's red plates), the dark grey structure becomes a mid grey worn bare-ish steel (as INPUT 2's grey structure, a little darker), bright rings stay brighter polished steel, recesses, vents and grilles stay near black, the canopy stays a dark cyan-tinted glass. Do not swap or invent colours, stripes, patches or markings.
- Finish: a front-line military fighter in good order. Crisp semi-matte enamel with fine plate seams, flush fastener rows and small access panels, subtle plate-to-plate tone differences. Light, even service wear only: faint edge scuffs on exposed corners and leading edges, a thin film of grime in seams, soot on the two drive drums at the stern. No rust, no chipped-away paint areas, no repair plates, no dents, no damage, no burns, no large stains, no lettering, numbers or insignia.
- Lighting: soft, even, nearly shadowless studio light from above, so every material reads at its true colour. No strong specular highlights, no reflections of an environment, no rim light, no dramatic shading.
Output: one landscape 16:9 image, same composition as INPUT 1.

references.role: INPUT 1: the render to repaint (layout authority)

agentMessages: I’ll use the image-generation tool to repaint Image 1, preserving its geometry and composition and using Image 2 only for the livery colours.
